checks: Compactness leaves finitely many input bases. At normalized level q>0 the selected fibers have positive volume and each level set is nonempty. A selected weighted tuple has an integral output base by hypothesis, and ordinary Brunn–Minkowski on its compact continuous fibers gives at least q times the dth power of the weighted peak-root sum.

A generic linear functional orders any two finite nonempty sets injectively. Traversing one set with the other initial point fixed, then traversing the other while fixing the former's last point, gives |U|+|V|−1 strictly increasing sums. Iterate for scaled inputs. Each output is counted once, irrespective of collisions, and the volume of its union is at least one witnessing Minkowski volume.

Integrating only thresholds through L^d gives the peak bound, since ∫_0^1 N_i(q)dq=M_i/a_i. The prefactor is at least each effective count M_i/a_i, so its dth root times each weighted peak root dominates that input's weighted total root.

For a zero-mass input choose an actual point. Its translation of the remaining weighted sum preserves fiber volumes, and the stronger all-nonempty-base hypothesis guarantees integrality after translation. The positive-input proof uses the original coefficients and only the number of positive inputs. All-zero masses and zero coefficients are covered separately.

For equal weights and step k on a primitive integer line, the output index set is a full interval of ΣN_i−k+1 sites. Every output fiber is the same homothetic sum of the fixed convex fibers. Independently enumerated the sums and checked the integer volume numerator in 24 cases with k=1,…,6 and d=1,…,4. One common input base reduces the root equality to ordinary homothetic Brunn–Minkowski.

For d=0 no volume root is used and the same distinct-sum argument gives cardinality. Convexity and affinity put the actual weighted set in the asserted original closed cap, including a pure-base cut carrying a full fiber on its boundary.

Checked 3d8aa8562dba80fc (1)–(3) and its cap paragraph, e7b862fa9bf72057 §§1–5, and 825f4248238fa3c9's compact-fiber comparison. The normalized proof subsumes the positive peak and the stronger-integrality zero-mass root scopes without relying on their pending status.

overlap.comparison: Uses ordinary Brunn–Minkowski for compact portions of one compatible family at a fixed weighted output in a common-scale weak slice limit. It does not sum over distinct integral outputs or give an input peak correction.

Counts off-diagonal midpoints within one same-parity set under rank-spread and quota conditions. It has a different restricted sum and does not give the multi-input peak law or the zero-mass extension.

readability: The hypotheses deliberately strengthen from positive-volume input bases for the peak law to all nonempty bases for the possibly zero-mass root law. The point-fixing argument explains the need for this distinction.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The level-set proof gives the weighted peak refinement, its zero-mass and counting extensions, and the stated exact equality families on integral output bases.
